title: Round467 first-five Max Damage intervention transfer check
summary: The Round467 policy with legal Max Damage choices replacing its first five battle decisions improved on four held-out opponents: paired gains were +7.62 pp [2.73, 12.50] vs Max Damage, +12.30 pp [7.32, 17.29] vs public Counterplay, +8.20 pp [3.42, 12.89] vs PPO Round464, and +8.98 pp [4.00, 13.87] vs PPO Round465. Heuristic results pool two independent 128-cluster seed sets; PPO tests use 256 clusters each.
method: Raw and hybrid arms used fixed teams, previews, repeat indices, and side-swapped games. Paired 95% intervals use 10,000 team-cluster bootstrap resamples. Showdown battle randomness is server-side and not identical between arms. All completed games had zero action corrections and timeouts; one raw Round465 case was incomplete and excluded from its matched comparison.
intervention: Use legal Max Damage joint actions for decision indices 0 through 4, then return control to the Round467 masked PPO policy.

opponents.source_set: 256 clusters; one raw case incomplete, 511 matched cases

interpretation: This is promising cross-opponent transfer for an inference-time hybrid, not PPO learning, broad-population robustness, or optimal-play evidence. The win-probability head was not used for action selection. Round430 remains the validated learned checkpoint; keep this hybrid experimental pending wider response audits and adapter validation.
next_step: Evaluate a wider policy league and fresh legal-response audits; then validate the override through the local Showdown adapter before changing default play.
runtime_note: Evaluation throughput on 8 workers: 7.38–9.95 games/s vs heuristic opponents and 5.35–6.78 games/s vs PPO policies. This is evaluation throughput, not training rollout throughput.
